value_or_angle: header="Princeton, then a Yale law degree" body="John taught military science and tactics at Princeton and retired from the Army in 1919. He then took a Yale law degree in 1923 and a doctorate in 1924, and came to Oklahoma City that year." category=education

value_or_angle: header="Broadlawns, northwest of Norman" body="John practised law briefly in Oklahoma City and in the Second World War headed its retired officers' bureau. From 1933 he and Ethel lived at Broadlawns, a country house northwest of Norman, where both of them died." category=family

value_or_angle: header="Colonial Dames president in Oklahoma" body="Raised and schooled in Dorchester and Boston, Ethel came to Oklahoma City in 1925 with her husband. She was a president of the Colonial Dames there and active in the Art League, the Rose Society and St. Paul's Episcopal Church." category=family

value_or_angle: header="His father gave Atlanta its zoo" body="John's father, George Valentine Gress, an Atlanta lumberman and Union veteran of the 56th Pennsylvania, bought a bankrupt circus south of Atlanta in 1887 and gave its animals to the city. They became the start of Zoo Atlanta." category=family
